title: Optimize Console: interactive cost-savings cards, staged-diff preview and rollback ledger
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Build a cohesive Console UX for Optimize that surfaces automated batching and caching recommendations as interactive cards, gives a safe staged-diff preview before applying changes to runtime configs, and records a tamper-evident rollback ledger (apply history + metadata) for audits and post-mortems.

Background: Teams running production workloads want automated unit-cost savings without risking regressions. Current backend recommendations exist (Optimize engine) but there is no standardized way in Console to review, stage, apply, and audit those config changes. This ticket unblocks a cross-functional rollout: design for recommendation cards + diff preview, API contract for staged applies, and backend persistence for an immutable apply ledger.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-apply safe batching/caching optimizations for customers by 40%.
- Provide a clear, explainable preview of the exact runtime config diffs and expected cost/latency impact.
- Ensure every apply action has an immutable record with actor, timestamp, pre/post config, metrics snapshot, and an easy rollback button.

Scope (in-scope):
- Recommendation card UI (ranked list, cost/latency delta, confidence score, example affected routes)
- Side-by-side staged-diff preview with inline risk annotations (e.g., increased latency probability, model-quality delta)
- Apply workflow: dry-run -> staged apply -> commit -> auto-monitoring guardrails (30m watch window)
- Apply ledger: append-only history view with CSV export and linkable audit IDs for compliance
- Compact server API endpoints to create/preview/apply/rollback recommendations

Out of scope: automated one-click global rollout to dedicated infra (follow-up ticket), advanced simulation of model quality when switching quantization profiles (research).

Design principles: minimize blast radius, make cost/quality trade-offs explicit, enable safe operator control, and produce auditable records for compliance teams.
acceptance_criteria: Recommendation cards display name, estimated monthly token cost delta, estimated p95 latency change, confidence score, affected routes (up to 5), and link to example traces.
Staged-diff preview shows exact JSON patch of runtime config with syntax highlighting and inline explanations for each changed field.
Users can run a dry-run which simulates cost delta and registers no change to runtime; simulation results are surfaced in UI within 30s for small workloads.
Apply workflow requires explicit confirmation, records actor and reason, and creates an immutable ledger entry including pre/post config, metrics snapshot, and an audit ID.
Rollback can revert the last committed staged apply within 90 minutes and records rollback metadata in the ledger.
All interactions are covered by automated E2E tests and manual QA checklist in Confluence.
Design handoff artifacts (Figma + tokens) and API contract documented and approved by ENG and Security.
comments: 2026-03-09 - Miguel: Kickoff meeting notes added. Agreed to keep apply guardrail at 30m watch window and require PM sign-off for P0 customers. Action: ENG to propose API schema by 2026-03-12.
2026-03-11 - Designer (Lina Wei): Uploaded initial card comps to Figma. Card variants include compact list + expanded details panel. Link: https://www.figma.com/file/OptimizeCards/Redwood-Optimize-UI

2026-03-11 - ENG (Ravi Singh): Proposed API endpoints: POST /optimize/preview, POST /optimize/stage, POST /optimize/commit, POST /optimize/rollback. Shared proto in GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/optimize/pull/198

2026-03-12 - Security (Jordan Kim): Requested threat model for apply ledger (tamper-evidence + retention policy). Adding KMS signature on ledger entries. Follow-up: ENG to include signature field and retention TTL in schema.
2026-03-12 - PM (Asha): Prioritized ledger CSV export & audit ID for SOC2 checklist. Customer compliance asked for export with filters by date/customer/model.

2026-03-13 - UX review (Design team): Decided to show cost delta as absolute dollars + percentage of monthly spend. Trade-off: more cognitive load vs clearer ROI signal. Chosen: show both with collapse option.

2026-03-13 - ENG (Miguel): Backend stub implemented for preview endpoint (internal branch). Load test shows preview latency ~150ms at 1k QPS when caching simulation enabled. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/472
risks: Applying batching/caching can introduce tail-latency regressions for certain low-batch workloads; guardrails and canarying required.
Ledger storage must be immutable for audits; integrating KMS/HSM signatures increases implementation complexity.
Over-surfacing recommendations may cause alert fatigue; need ranking and confidence thresholds.

audit_requirements: Ledger entries must include: audit_id, actor_email, timestamp, pre_config_hash, post_config_hash, metrics_snapshot (p50/p95 token latency, error rate), reason_text, KMS_signature. Retention: 7 years for enterprise customers per compliance request. CSV export must include filters for date range, actor, and customer.
estimated_savings_metric: Projected median customer savings: 12% monthly token cost (varies by workload). Estimated risk of latency regression >5ms p95 for 8% of recommended changes (requires monitoring).
